'''[[Khun Ying]] Thongtip Ratanarat''' ({{langx|th|ทองทิพ รัตนะรัต}}, {{RTGS|Thongthip Ratanarat}}; born 24 June 1942)<ref name="vita">[http://conference.tgo.or.th/download/tgo_or_th/Board/Board_Profile/Khunying_Thongtip.pdf Vita of Khunying Thonghip Ratanarat] (Thai)</ref> is a Thai chemical engineer. She is a member of the board of directors of [[Siam Chemicals#The Siam Fine Chemicals|The Siam Fine Chemicals]] and of the Foundation for the [[Petroleum Institute of Thailand]] (PTIT). From 1985 to 2005 she was the PTIT's executive director.

== Life and work ==

After completing her studies in [[chemical engineering]], Khunying Thongtip Ratanarat became a research assistant at the [[University of Canterbury]] in [[Christchurch]], [[New Zealand]]. When she returned to Thailand, she worked as a lecturer in chemical engineering at [[Chulalongkorn University]] in [[Bangkok]]. She was awarded an honorary doctorate in applied geophysics from [[Chiang Mai University]] in 2005.<ref name="vita"/> She also received an honorary PhD in chemical engineering from [[Kasetsart University]] for her work in 2013.<ref>[http://news.ku.ac.th/?p=1053 KU News: มหาวิทยาลัยเกษตรศาสตร์ มอบปริญญากิตติมศักดิ์ แก่ผู้ทรงคุณวุฒิ ในพิธีพระราชทานปริญญาบัตร ประจำปี 2556] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119142025/http://news.ku.ac.th/?p=1053 |date=2015-11-19 }} (Thai).</ref>

From 1985 to 2005 she was executive director of the [[Petroleum Institute of Thailand]]. Subsequently, she worked as an advisor to the [[PTT Public Company Limited|PTT Public Co., Ltd]].<ref>[http://www.tgo.or.th/english/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=23:board-of-directors&catid=25:about-tgo&Itemid=28 Thailand Greenhouse Gas Management Organization (Public Organization).] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119070516/http://www.tgo.or.th/english/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=23:board-of-directors&catid=25:about-tgo&Itemid=28 |date=2015-11-19 }}</ref> She is Member of the Board of Directors of [[Siam Chemicals#The Siam Fine Chemicals|The Siam Fine Chemicals]].<ref>[http://www.siamchemicals.co.th/sfc_company_profile/thesiamfinechemicalsprofile.pdf Company Profile: The Siam Fine Chemicals.]</ref> She was judge of the Platts Global Energy Awards in 2004, 2011 and 2013.<ref>Platts, McGraw Hill Financial: [https://online.platts.com/PPS/P=m&s=1029337384756.1478827&e=1109179543321.3211354954247070912/?artnum=20GI0OT50Wi21M01K05202_1 The 2004 Global Energy Awards.]</ref><ref>[http://www.platts.ru/IM.Platts.Content%5Caboutplatts%5Cmediacenter%5Cgeaprogram2011.pdf Platts Global Energy Awards 2011: Recognizing the Stars of the Global Energy Industry]</ref> She was the chairperson of the committee investigating the [[Rayong oil spill|2013 Rayong oil spill]].<ref>[http://www.bangkokpost.com/learning/learning-from-news/364740/oil-spill-panel-says-pttgc-not-at-fault Oil spill: Panel says PTTGC was not at fault.] Bangkok Post, 15 August 2013.</ref> She is also a member of the national advisory board of the [[Chulabhorn Research Institute]] in Bangkok<ref>[https://www.cri.or.th/en/about_bc_nation_advisory.php National Advisory Board of the Chulabhorn Research Institute].</ref> and director emeritus of the Circum-Pacific Council for Energy and Mineral Resources.<ref>[http://www.circum-pacificcouncil.org/about/officers-directors Officers and Directors of the Circum-Pacific Council for Energy and Mineral Resources.]</ref>

Thongtip has sung with King [[Bhumibol Adulyadej]]'s ''Au Saw Friday Band''.<ref>{{Citation |url=http://thailand.prd.go.th/ebook2/king_music/king_music.html |title=The Au Saw Friday Band: A History |work=King Bhumibol Adulyadej and Music |publisher=The Government Public Relations Department |accessdate=6 November 2015}}</ref> She has been a [[lady-in-waiting]] to Queen [[Sirikit]] since 1973.<ref>{{Citation |url=http://www.ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/DATA/PDF/2516/D/100/2331.PDF |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304083145/http://www.ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/DATA/PDF/2516/D/100/2331.PDF |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |title=ประกาศสำนักพระราชวัง เรื่อง ทรงพระกรุณาโปรดเกล้าฯ ให้นางทองทิพย์ รัตนะรัต เป็นนางสนองพระโอษฐ์ |journal=Royal Thai Government Gazette |volume=90 |number=100 |date=7 August 1973 |page=2331}}</ref>

== Development of biofuels ==

During her career she encouraged the local production of natural gas and focussed particularly on the development of biofuels, to overcome the volatility of the petroleum market. By 2002 she observed that ‘vulnerability is the rule of the game’ due to instability and tension in the Middle East and the related terrorism threats. In terms of self-reliance Europe and Asia were therefore following the U.S. in looking for deriving energy from other sources.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20151122174703/http://www.nationmultimedia.com/business/OIL-PRICES-Volatility-expected-to-get-worse-61630.html Oil prices: Volatility expected to get worse.]</ref> In 2004 she noted that Thailand needs a master plan to maximise the value of locally produced natural gas.<ref>[http://www.gasandoil.com/news/south_east_asia/e01cd03f5b313495385db3045891a862 Thailand to invest in 33 petrochemical projects.]</ref> In 2012 she was quoted as saying: ‘We should get more serious about joint development of biofuels as, in the future, oil prices will definitely increase. It will also help strengthen the Asean Economic Community as we could all grow, blend, sell and consume by ourselves’.<ref>[http://biofuels-news.com/display_news/5105/Thai_energy_advocates_call_for_biofuels_investment/ Thai energy advocates call for biofuels investment.]</ref> She urged the government to encourage the use of [[E20 fuel|E20]] and [[E85]] ethanol blended fuel among Thai motorists.<ref>[http://www.ssig.gov.my/blog/2012/06/27/thai-government-urged-to-promote-ethanol-use/ Thai Government Urged To Promote Ethanol Use.]</ref>

== Family ==

She is a sister of [[Thongchat Hongladarom]], the first governor of [[PTT Public Company Limited|PTT]], when it was still a state enterprise.<ref>Wasant Techawongtham: [http://www.bangkokpost.com/print/367086/ Oil spill panel fails to win over public trust.] Bangkok Post, 30 August 2013.</ref>

She married in 1969 [[Chira Ratanarat]], who is now the [[chief executive officer]] of [[Siam Chemicals|The Siam Chemicals Public Company (SCC)]], and has with him three sons: Tisanu Ratanarat (born 1974), Sichart Ratanarat (born 1976) and Porapong Ratanarat (born 1982).<ref>[http://consulsthailand.org/countries.php?id=57 นายจิระ  รัตนะรัต: กงสุลกิตติมศักดิ์ราชอาณาจักรโมร็อกโกประจำประเทศไทย Honorary Consul of the Kingdom Morocco to the Kingdom of Thailand.]</ref>
